results.corrected_title: Lovable rolls out enterprise controls: EU inference and deployment in customers' own AWS and Azure accounts
results.corrected_summary: In one week Lovable published a series of enterprise announcements. On 12 October it added an EU inference setting for Enterprise customers that sends supported AI model requests to European endpoints. On 14 October it launched Deploy on AWS in private preview, which lets companies run Lovable apps, databases and storage inside their own AWS account, and Deutsche Telekom went live with it in October. Deploy on Azure followed on 15 October, also in private preview, together with new growth tools and expanded third-party AI model support.
key_facts: EU inference (12 Oct): Enterprise-only setting that sends supported model requests to European endpoints. It covers model processing only, not full data residency, and web tools still process data in the US.
Deploy on AWS (14 Oct): private preview for select Enterprise customers. Apps run in a dedicated VPC in the customer's own AWS account (EKS, Lambda, Aurora PostgreSQL, S3).
Deutsche Telekom went live in October with its Lovable apps running in its own AWS account.
Deploy on Azure (15 Oct): private preview, apps run in the customer's own Azure subscription.
14 Oct: growth tools to help users find customers. 15 Oct: more third-party AI models and tools available in the apps users build.
Lovable said it passed $600M in annualized run-rate revenue on 24 Sept 2026 (TechCrunch). This was before the 9-18 Oct window.
results.issues: The '>$600m ARR' figure was announced on 24 Sept 2026, before the window; background only. 'Bring-your-own models' is not confirmed. The Azure details come only from the blog index; the Azure post itself was not opened. All of these are company announcements.

results.corrected_title: Stordalen buys into two AI-focused companies and says Strawberry will invest 'hundreds of millions' in AI
results.corrected_summary: Petter Stordalen has bought 70% of ad-film company Verk and 35% of AI consultancy Spinner through Storm, a PR agency in his agency network, E24 reported on 17 October 2026. The price was not disclosed. AI company Prosper Group is also a co-owner of Spinner. Stordalen told E24 that Strawberry Group will spend 'hundreds of millions' on AI in its companies over the coming years, and that AI will not mean fewer employees.
key_facts: 70% stake in Verk, an ad-film company that uses AI to make human-made films more efficient (founder Mari Grundnes Paus).
35% stake in Spinner, an AI consultancy (founder Simon Isaksen). Prosper Group is a co-owner.
Both stakes were bought through Storm, part of Stordalen's agency network alongside Smeh and Smør. The price is secret.
Strawberry Group plans to spend 'hundreds of millions' on AI in its companies over the coming years.
Stordalen says AI will not reduce headcount but will let staff do more with greater precision.
results.issues: Only one source (E24). Small wording fix: the article says AI will not mean fewer employees, which is stronger than the candidate's 'doesn't expect many job cuts'.

results.corrected_title: Oslo startup Solvera raises $6.3m pre-seed to build an AI-native engineering firm
results.corrected_summary: Solvera, an Oslo company founded in 2026, has raised a $6.3 million pre-seed round led by Seedcamp. It sells finished engineering work for construction rather than software licences or hourly consulting. AI agents do the work on its own operating system, supervised by human engineers, starting with mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) design. Contractor Betonmast has chosen Solvera for several projects, and the money will fund a London office as well as growth in Oslo.
key_facts: Other investors: Construct Venture, Inception Fund, Momentum, OBOS Ventures, PSV Tech, Sondo and The Nordic Web Ventures.
Angel investors include Spacemaker founders Anders Kvåle and Håvard Haukeland, plus former OBOS CEO Daniel Kjørberg Siraj (BeBeez).
Founders: Arif Mirza (CEO), Pål Eskild Rasmussen (CTO) and Thorvald Thorsnes (CCO). Founded in 2026.
Starts with MEP engineering. Betonmast has chosen Solvera for several projects, including commercial ones.
The funding will pay for a London office, a bigger Oslo team and further work on its operating system.
results.issues: No material problems. The 2026 founding year is confirmed by BeBeez, not Tech.eu.
